answer: One defense is an anchored commitment with delayed reveal: each new agent locks a hashed identity commitment plus a small bond in a shared vault, and only after a fixed waiting period may it reveal the preimage and become a vertex in the trust graph. Since every identity must sit idle while bonded, a Sybil attacker cannot conjure thousands of accounts on demand; each one costs locked capital and calendar time, and any later proven to share an operator forfeit their bonds. Honest newcomers lose almost nothing, so the economy remains a haven for them while mass fakery grows expensive.
